claims.value: Le Noble gives side A an army reduced to 20,000 combatants before the advance on Porto, not all necessarily at the final assault.
claims.rationale: Approach army population; detached/engaged subset remains unresolved. English rendering (ours): "So many enemies and obstacles confronted an army reduced to twenty thousand combatants."

claims.value: Le Noble reports side B’s gathering estimated at 60,000 regulars, militia and armed inhabitants/Ordenanzas before the assault.
claims.rationale: Opponent estimate of a growing mixed gathering, not a count of combatants actually defending the line; not added to civilian city population. English rendering (ours): "At Porto the gathering was already estimated at sixty thousand regular troops, militia, and armed inhabitants or national guards called Ordenanzas."

claims.value: Toreno says the bishop abandoned the city before the attack and substituted General Parreiras; Le Noble describes episcopal chief command with Portuguese lieutenants.
claims.rationale: Effective local replacement versus overall title remains a source/timing question; no sole-credit inference. English rendering (ours): "The bishop commanded in chief but left the city on the eve of the attack, placing General Parreiras in his stead; [Le Noble] calls the bishop chief with Perela and de Lima as lieutenants."

claims.value: Le Noble describes an entrenched camp of closed palisaded works, trenches and abatis outside an open city.
claims.rationale: Actual described works; open city does not imply undefended surrounding position. English rendering (ours): "The various entrenchments were linked by palisaded ditches and abatis."

claims.value: Le Noble transmits Soult’s order placing the chief at the central attack.
claims.rationale: An order specifies intended command location; it is not a synchronized observation of continuous presence. English rendering (ours): "The marshal commanding in chief will remain at the central attack."
